subject: Activity records immutability & export — VSQ kickoff
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@neuromed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Activity records immutability & export — VSQ kickoff

Alex — great speaking earlier. Short recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can keep the security review moving.

Call highlights (as I captured):
- NeuroMed needs admin activity logs + API request logs for user/admin actions, retention 3+ years (regulatory).
- You asked about exportability (direct S3 export, CSV/NDJSON preferred) and whether logs can be delivered immutable/write-once.
- Regulatory scope: HIPAA for clinical data and GDPR for EU users — you want evidence of controls and an initial VSQ run.

Action items / asks:
1) Can you attach the NeuroMed VSQ (I think Liz will share) so we can start pre-filling answers?
2) Please confirm your preferred export format: CSV, NDJSON, or both, and if you require push to your S3 account or a signed export.
3) Confirm if immutability must be enforced at the object store level (S3 Object Lock) or if an append-only export with audit chain is sufficient.

What I can do immediately:
- Loop in our security/ops to draft a short technical note on what we expose today (admin events, API logs, retention/exports) and what requires change (if any).
- Provide a pre-populated VSQ answers draft + evidence bundle link for your review.

Attached: connor-postcall-notes.pdf (brief recap)

Propose a 30-min security sync next week to walk the VSQ answers and any technical evidence. I’m available Tue/Wed 9–11 PT.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@neuromed.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Liz Price <liz.price@neuromed.com>, NeuroMed IT <it@neuromed.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Activity records immutability & export — VSQ kickoff

Thanks Connor — appreciate the recap. Attaching the NeuroMed VSQ (PDF) — Liz is copied. Quick clarifications from our security team:

- Preferred export: NDJSON to our S3 bucket (we can provide a presigned upload or an ingest role). CSV is useful for ad-hoc reports but not our canonical export.
- Immutability: we prefer S3 Object Lock with Governance/Compliance mode for regulatory auditability. If you can provide an export path that writes to a locked bucket under our control, that meets our bar.
- Required logs: admin activity (console and admin API), API request logs (including request/response metadata), and a chain of custody indicating when exports were generated and by whom.
- SOC 2: we need to confirm Redwood's current SOC 2 status (Type II preferred) and any available evidence.

We can start the VSQ now — sending the PDF. Can your security team pre-fill section 2 (Logging & Monitoring) and share evidence pointers (screenshots/config snippets)?

Thanks — can do a 30-min sync Wed 10 PT if that works for your team.

Best,
Alex
Head of IT Integrations
NeuroMed Inc.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: NeuroMed VSQ + export/immutability questions

Connor/Marissa — quick technical answers and recommended next steps below. I’ve also attached a draft of pre-filled VSQ answers and an evidence bundle for common items.

What we have today (high-level):
- Log types: admin activity logs (console logins, admin role changes, permission updates), API request logs (request metadata, timestamps, authenticated principal, model id, route), and system events (service restarts, autoscaler events). We record request/response metadata but redact user PII in stored request bodies by default unless customer enables full payload capture.
- Export formats: NDJSON and CSV available. Exports can be generated on-demand and streamed to a customer S3 bucket via presigned PUTs or by writing to a bucket ARN we have access to (prefers presigned for security).
- Immutability: We can support customer-side S3 Object Lock if the export is written directly into their bucket with Object Lock enabled. Where direct writes aren't possible, we offer an append-only export package with a signed manifest (hash chain) and timestamped attestations.
- Retention: Retention windows configurable per account; default retention is 90 days, supports custom policies up to 7 years (policy needs commit during onboarding).
- Evidence / SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II in Q4 2026. We can share the report under NDA and provide a CSV of relevant controls mapping for the VSQ.

Suggested next steps:
1) Connor/Marissa: schedule the 30-min security sync (Wed 10 PT is fine for us).
2) I’ll push a pre-filled VSQ draft (redwood-vsq-answers-draft.pdf) and a short evidence bundle link (redwood_evidence_bundle.zip placeholder) so Alex/Liz can review.
3) If NeuroMed requires writes into a locked S3 bucket, request their bucket ARN and confirm Object Lock settings; we’ll validate with infra and confirm any additional work required.

Attachments: redwood-vsq-answers-draft.pdf, redwood_evidence_bundle.zip

Rishi Malhotra
Security Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference
